title: Canonical trivialization of absolute Frobenius pullback
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p>0$. On its
small pro-etale site, the
derived pullback
along absolute $p$-power Frobenius $F_X$ has a canonical
trivialization $LF_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. It commutes with
restriction to open subschemes and with its multiplicative iterates.
(Source for the input: [Stacks,
Tag 0F6W](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F6W), label `lemma-relative-frobenius-weakly-etale` – for a weakly etale $U\to X$ the relative
Frobenius $F_{U/X}:U\to U\times_{X,F_X}X$ is an isomorphism; the
trivialization of the derived pullback and its compatibilities with
restriction and with the iterates are the content of the proof below.)

note: *Recorded in advance* from chapter *The trace formula* of the source.

proof.text: Construct r on a weakly etale object V over X as the pullback lift (F_V^n, v). The naturality of iterated absolute Frobenius proves both its compatibility with the structure map and its naturality in V. Obtain the characteristic of V by applying v on global sections.

source.place: Paragraph 4, relative Frobenius and adjoint trivialization with its restriction and iterate compatibilities

proof.text: Every characteristic-p scheme has a map to Spec of the prime field. Specialize the finite-field universal-homeomorphism theorem at exponent one, and then use composition to obtain all iterates. The first projection of the pullback is a universal homeomorphism. Cancel it from r followed by that projection, which is absolute Frobenius on V. Thus r is a universal homeomorphism; it is weakly etale by cancellation from its composite with the second projection. The weakly-etale universal-homeomorphism criterion proves r is an isomorphism.

source.place: Paragraph 4, relative Frobenius and adjoint trivialization with its restriction and iterate compatibilities

proof.text: Apply the proved arbitrary-ring theorem [lem-pur-proetale-module-pullback-composition]. Its direct-image comparison is normalized on every section by the fibre-product composition isomorphism, and its pullback comparison is fixed by conjugation through the specified module adjunctions. Select this comparison for each pair of morphisms; the conjugation equation gives exactly the required section normalization.

source.place: Paragraph 4, relative Frobenius and adjoint trivialization with its restriction and iterate compatibilities

proof.text: Restriction along r identifies Frobenius pushforward of constant-ring modules with the identity: its coefficient map becomes the identity by the sheafification calculation. Conjugating the inverse isomorphism gives tau from module pullback to the identity. The unit equation for conjugation gives precisely the required section formula involving r inverse.

source.place: Paragraph 4, relative Frobenius and adjoint trivialization with its restriction and iterate compatibilities

proof.text: For a scheme map, compare the two relative Frobenius lifts after the standard iterated-pullback identifications. Their first projections agree by naturality of Frobenius and their second projections by the over-category structure equations, so pullback uniqueness proves equality. Restricting a module sheaf along the inverse maps proves the normalized pushforward square sectionwise. Injectivity of adjunction conjugation gives the pullback square. Apply this with an open immersion.

source.place: Paragraph 4, relative Frobenius and adjoint trivialization with its restriction and iterate compatibilities

proof.text: The projection equations likewise identify the composite of the relative Frobenius lifts for a and b with the lift for a+b, using the power law for absolute Frobenius. Invert this equality, apply module restriction maps, and conjugate to obtain the pullback product law. The lift for zero is the pullback identity comparison, again by its projections. Finally transport the ordinary natural-isomorphism equalities to exact derived functors using the library mapDerivedCategoryNatIso composition and whiskering coherence lemmas. This gives the specified derived open square and iterate formula without K-flat resolutions.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme in characteristic $p>0$. On its
small pro-etale site, the
derived pullback
along absolute $p$-power Frobenius $F_X$ has a canonical
trivialization $LF_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. It commutes with
restriction to open subschemes and with its multiplicative iterates.

proof.text:
An object $v:V\to X$ of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] is weakly
etale. Its relative Frobenius is

$$
r_V=(F_V,v):V\longrightarrow V\times_{X,F_X}X.
$$

It is integral and universally bijective. For an affine ring map
$R\to B$, the corresponding map
$B\otimes_{R,F_R}R\to B$ sends $b\otimes a$ to $b^pv(a)$.
Every $b\in B$ satisfies the monic equation $T^p-b^p=0$ over the
image, proving integrality. For an algebraically closed field
$\Omega$, a homomorphism from the tensor product to $\Omega$
specifies maps $\beta:B\to\Omega$, $\alpha:R\to\Omega$ satisfying
$\beta(v(a))=\alpha(a)^p$. The unique lift to $B$ is
$b\mapsto\beta(b)^{1/p}$: it is a ring map and its restriction to
$R$ is $\alpha$. This proves universal bijectivity. The argument
is local on $X$ and $V$, so $r_V$ is a universal homeomorphism.

Its source and target are weakly etale over $X$; the target is a
base change of $v$. Thus [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects]
shows that $r_V$ is weakly etale. For clarity, the geometric
factorization behind this Mathlib result is as follows. If
$f:U\to W$ is a map between weakly etale $X$-schemes, its graph
$\Gamma_f:U\to U\times_XW$ is the base change of
$\Delta_{W/X}$ along
$(f\circ\operatorname{pr}_U,\operatorname{pr}_W)$, so is flat.
The projection $U\times_XW\to W$ is flat as a base change of
$U\to X$. Their composite $f$ is flat. Moreover the square

$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
U&\xrightarrow{\operatorname{id}}&U\\
{\scriptstyle\Delta_f}\downarrow&&
\downarrow{\scriptstyle\Delta_{U/X}}\\
U\times_WU&\longrightarrow&U\times_XU
\end{array}
$$

is Cartesian: on a test scheme a point of its fiber product is
$(u,(u_1,u_2))$ with $(u,u)=(u_1,u_2)$, hence is uniquely
$(u,(u,u))$. Therefore $\Delta_f$ is flat as well. These are
exactly the flatness conditions in
[def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].
Applying [lem-trf-weakly-etale-homeomorphism] now makes
$r_V$ an isomorphism.

The $r_V$ commute with all morphisms of site objects. Consequently
the base-change functor $V\mapsto V\times_{X,F_X}X$ is naturally
isomorphic to the identity and preserves its coverings. On sheaves,
the inverses of the restriction maps along $r_V$ give
$\mathcal F(V)\simeq(F_{X*}\mathcal F)(V)$. Taking left adjoints
gives $F_X^*\simeq\operatorname{id}$. Both functors are exact,
so the same maps on complexes give the derived assertion with
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Restricting the maps
$r_V$ to an open gives the same relative Frobenius there.
Composing them gives relative $p^m$-power Frobenius, proving the
restriction and iteration assertions.
